checks.text: No order that doubles the cell: no zone-boundary point stands out of the diffuse background (the strongest, Ta at (0, 0, ½), is 0.9× the median, < −8σ after the correction).
Ta's strongest mode is a long-wavelength wave, q = (0.1, 0.2, -0.1) at 13× the median: box-scale displacement correlations (common in RMC), not a crystallographic superstructure.

Ta displacements are correlated in phase between neighbouring cells (+0.11 between cells [0 1 0] apart, > 8σ against independent cells): the power beyond the long waves leans toward the zone centre — neighbouring cells moving together (correlated motion; as RMC's long waves and acoustic-like thermal motion give), not order.

data.note: zone_boundary rows are [q, ratio, percentile, sigma]: an element's displacement power at wavevector q (fractions of the cell's reciprocal axes) over its median across all q of the supercell grid (the diffuse background), the share of the compared modes (one per ±q pair, long waves with every |q_i| ≤ 0.25 left out) with less power, and the calibrated one-sided significance against independent cells (each cell's own correlations kept), corrected over all 21 zone-boundary points of the configuration's 3 elements, whichever the call names (≥ 3 with ratio ≥ 3 is order). strongest rows are [q, ratio, percentile, sigma]: the sigma of a general q (neither zone boundary nor long wave; a complex sum, corrected over the compared modes of every element), null otherwise. A ½ component is order that doubles the cell along that axis; order at a general q is correlation between cells (incommensurate or short-range) that does not. diffuse is [lag, correlation, sigma]: the strongest correlation between a site's displacements in cells one lag apart that the power over the compared modes shows (+ in phase, − antiphase), and the significance of the 13 neighbour-cell lags together against independent cells (≥ 3 with |correlation| ≥ 0.1: correlation spread over many q).
